matrix_reconciliation.matrix_pass_is_runtime_or_static: RUNTIME artifact, and structurally over-claimed. The matrix is a runtime-generated CSV (census: 973 CSVs under tests/_runtime/ ui_test_matrix_*.csv). Rows are emitted from source as status=planned (act_* from MainWindow.cpp, dialog-widget from audit_source.py) then flipped green/red at runtime by conftest.record_matrix_result(). The committed 'green' reflects a one-off developer-workstation interactive run, NOT a reproducible CI result — on the Server-2019 runner the backing pywinauto tests skip (gap_a14). Row color is also a fragile last-write-wins value (tests/ui_automation/conftest.py:85 MATRIX_RESULTS[test_id]=... ; sessionfinish:575), so a non-owning suite's SKIP could clobber a proven GREEN. Prior audit already found the matrix structurally over-claimed (a runtime CSV rebuilt from committed green).

visual_verification_is_shallow_because: CHANGE-DETECTION, not correctness: _assert_canvas_changed only proves SOMETHING changed (SSIM dropped OR pixels differ). A canvas rendered mirrored/blurry/wrong-zoom/wrong-rotation still trips 'changed' and passes — there is no golden of the CORRECT result to diff against for most rows.

GOLDEN SELF-SEEDING: first run with no committed golden calls regen_golden(force=False) then compares the just-captured image against itself — zero delta, always pass. On a fresh runner (no source-controlled golden) the 'compare' protects nothing (test_ui_harness_smoke.py:183-208).

THRESHOLDS RELAXED TO 0.85 and many file-ops rows are explicitly annotated 'VISUAL: no' (net-zero pixel change by design; native-shell dialogs excluded as OS-chrome), so large swaths of the file-ops suite carry no pixel oracle at all.
ALL visual asserts sit behind REQUIRES_LIVE_UI + the gap_a14 UIA/dialog skips — so in the Server-2019 CI they do not execute; visual protection exists only on a developer workstation.
invisible_regression_classes: Canvas renders the page MIRRORED or rotated the wrong direction — change-detector sees a diff and passes; no correct-orientation golden.
Canvas renders at the WRONG ZOOM / wrong tile scale — half-size or double-size content still differs from baseline = 'changed' = pass.

Glyphs render as .notdef/tofu or blurry while text still EXTRACTS correctly — extraction-blind (phase-1 systemic 'extraction-only-for-visual'); UI layer has no glyph-ink oracle except the single per-line-font-size probe.

A control/toolbar button renders but paints the WRONG icon or WRONG color — objectName-exists / reachability oracle is blind to pixels (annotation toolbar has NO icons at all per UI_MATRIX_GAPS UI-AN-22, undetectable).
A dialog OPENS but its contents are garbled/mislaid-out — the 236 dialog-reachability rows assert only that the objectName exists in source, never that it renders.

White/invisible/half-size edited text in the content stream (the exact shipped mirror/half-size/color-loss bug class) — no UI pixel oracle catches it; only the C++ content-stream tests (also extraction-blind) cover it.
Wrong-but-plausible rendered content in a region — no committed golden to compare against (self-seeded), so a plausible-looking wrong render is indistinguishable from correct.
visual_oracle_critique.cross_reference_phase1: Phase-1 oracle synthesis: widget-exists-only smell in 77 files, EXPECT_NO_THROW-only in 81, extraction-only-for-visual in 71; weak-oracle (proxy+no-oracle-smoke) = 147/402 files (36.6%). The systemic_pattern note names extraction-only-for-visual as 'the dominant cross-cluster disease ... structurally blind to mirror/invisible/white/wrong-glyph/half-size/off-page'. The UI layer's structural (objectName/signal/dialog-open) oracles are the same disease one level up: real render, no render oracle.
